standout_why: I read projectorverdict.com, projectorcentral.com/best-church-projectors.htm, the Panasonic House of Worship guide and itechguides.com. Projectorverdict only gives lumen bands and one short-throw distance, with nothing on cable runs or power. ProjectorCentral lists ISO lumens and one throw range, says nothing about cable runs or HDBaseT, and only mentions power as 'can run on 120 volts' for a 20,000-lumen model. Panasonic gives a rule of thumb (match lumens to screen area and add about 20% headroom) but no numbers for distance or power. itechguides lists 'HDBaseT' in a spec table and says a long cable run 'may require a suitable signal-transport solution', but gives no limit in feet or meters. The BenQ PDF would not render as readable text. None of them put a number on how far HDMI can run between the booth and the projector, which is the fact that decides the third item in the kit.
kit_items: Projector: Epson PowerLite L690U (6,500 lumens, WUXGA, laser). ChatGPT already showed it. Its 1.35–2.20 throw ratio puts a 150-inch 16:10 image anywhere from 14.3 to 23.3 ft back, so it fits most mid-size rooms without an optional lens. It has an HDBaseT RJ-45 input.

Signal link from booth to projector: AV Access 4KEX70-H2 HDBaseT extender kit. It sends 1080p 60 m (197 ft) over Cat5e/6 or 70 m (230 ft) over Cat6a, compared with 15 m (49 ft) for plain HDMI. One power supply at either end powers both units.
Cable: Category 5e STP or better (Cat6a for the full 70 m), cut to the measured booth-to-ceiling route.
Power at the mount: one ordinary 120 V outlet is enough. 415 W ÷ 120 V = 3.46 A, well under a 15 A circuit.
